pages.title: File:Unlimited Horizons - Design and Development of the U-2.pdf

ObjectName.value: Unlimited Horizons - Design and Development of the U-2

Categories.value: Lockheed U-2|PD NASA|Operation IceBridge|2015 books from the United States|Books from the United States PDF files|NASA Aeronautics Book Series|English-language PDF files

ImageDescription.value: Over the span of more than six decades, the U-2 evolved from a relatively basic, high-altitude camera platform for performing clandestine reconnaissance missions into a complex, multisensor platform that has been adapted for a multitude of civil and military roles. Variants in more than a dozen configurations have been used for intelligence gathering, strategic and tactical reconnaissance, communications relay, battle-damage assessment, treaty monitoring and verification, disaster relief, environmental and Earth resources studies, and a wide variety of scientific research. Born of a Cold War necessity to maintain the balance of power between East and West, the U-2 now serves equally well as a high-altitude tool for tracking terrorists in the mountains of Afghanistan or for tracking the migration of destructive spruce bark beetles through the forests of Alaska.

Credit.value: http://www.nasa.gov/connect/ebooks/unlimited_horizons_detail.html

pages.title: File:California Deputy Shoots Suspect Holding Man Hostage With Knife.webm

ObjectName.value: California Deputy Shoots Suspect Holding Man Hostage With Knife

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|PD California|Uploaded with video2commons|Police bodycam footage

ImageDescription.value: Bakersfield, California — The Kern County Sheriff’s Office released footage of a deputy fatally shooting a suspect after he threatened to kill an elderly man. On February 9th, deputies were called to the area of Pierce and State roads in Oildale on a report of a man "breaking car windows and committing assault with a deadly weapon." That weapon turned out to be a hunting knife. The suspect was later identified as 25-year-old Deven Karl Moore. Around 1:21 p.m. deputies located Moore walking northbound on Pierce Road telling him to “stop and drop the knife and drop the fire extinguisher”, but he did not obey commands from the deputies. Moore fled to a nearby guard shack at a business in the area and took a man hostage at knifepoint. It was at that point that Deputy Austin Burgess fired twice into the shack, killing Moore who was pronounced dead at the scene.
